SCHOOL SPORT TOUR SCAM

By: Nicky Troll | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
A travel agent specialising in international school sports tours leaves at four groups stranded this December with no flights and no accommodation.

Unique Selling Point:
UPSET PARENTS & DISTRAUGHT CHILDREN IN TEARS
LEKKER CROOK WITH OPPORTUNITY FOR A GOOD CONFRONT

Summary:
Vision Sport bills itself as an established and reliable sport/academic tour operator and sport event planner that specializes in the planning and professional execution of the logistics of group travel. A one-stop travel shop.

EXCEPT…. They’ve just cancelled 4 different tours, all in for over a R1 million each! Not reliable if you ask me.

We speak to kids who’s dreams have been shattered and track down the man that is responsible behind Vision Sport.

Further information:
Michael Byneveldt is behind Vision Sport. The company has been operating since 2014. And a number of tours have taken place. But it hasn’t been smooth sailing in 2019.

Tours started getting cancelled in mid-year:
 First an athletics tour to Switzerland. R40k per kid. Cancelled three days before departure in June 2019. Refunds never materialised.
 Then a cricket tour to Sri Lanka also set for June/July 2019. R30700 per kid. This time not cancelled, but postponed because of the April bombings to December 2019 – cancelled a month ago.
 Three groups set to depart now this week – two rugby groups and a hockey group. Each group paid in over R1 million! None of them will be departing.

INSIDER
I spoke to an employee. She doesn’t want to be interviewed. Says there isn’t enough money in the bank accounts to pay for the tours and that the trips definitely won’t go ahead. Her theory is that Byneveldt is a bad businessman and that he has been under quoting to get the business and then ran into trouble because he had to take from Peter to pay Paul. One of case studies has also spoken to her can relay the story. I have an audio recording.

Michael Byneveldt on the other hand likes to blame his clients:

“I have decided to close down Vision Sport with immediate effect. It was a very difficult decision to make, considering all the lives that will be effected by this decision.
I will be consulting with our lawyers regarding the legal processes we need to follow to get all outstanding bills paid and to make sure the uncorrupted people gets refunded what is left over after the process.
It has been a very taxing past 6 years and I have learnt that people are the most unpredictable source of life on this place we call earth.
May God be with those who stabbed me and wanted to see me fall. Those who took my kindness for weakness. I forgive you. Thanks to those who held my hand.
Even when it went tough.
I will stand up.
With you and for you.
Michael Beyneveldt”

On Sunday he sent another message:
“Good morning.
I have received good movement and support in the past 24 hours regarding the company and how we can save this situation. Vision Sport will still trade as per normal and not be closed down.
Unfortunately the tours are ruined, but we are going to see how we can postpone the tours or refund the players after calculating all losses by payments made to service providers.
I will be in contact with each one of the parents this week to discuss the options.
Best regards
Michael”

*I HAVE A SECRETLY FILMED VIDEO CLIP OF HIM EXPLAINING HIMSELF TO SOME OF THE PARENTS TAKEN ON THURSDAY

WE KNOW WHERE HE IS, HE WILL WANT TO TELL HIS SIDE OF THE STORY BECAUSE
HE SAYS PEOPLE DIDN’T PAY ON TIME… BUT THAT’s NOT TRUE

CASE STUDY 1: BARCO SMIT GROUP REPRESNETATIVE – NOORDVAAL RUGBY GROUP TO ARGENTINA
 23 kids (15/16 years), 3 parents. Departure – 2 December, Return – 11 December
 R32400 - 12 November had pay in R5000 – price went up R37400
 VISION SPORT blamed parents for not making payment deadlines in a mail on the 18th of October – but after collating all the proof of payments – the parents were actually R40k over on the milestone at that date.
 PAID UP IN FULL – accept for R8900 outstanding from two parents. BUT one child got injured and cancelled after paying R25k – so the tour was technically paid up. Cancelled on the 27th November
 got NOTHING – no flight, no accommodation
o Paid a small deposit for flights to Flight Centre – R9600 still due per person – Flight centre cancelled booking.
o Team uniforms and clothing not paid – spoke to supplier
o Accommodation not paid – parents spoke to hotels
 Promised refunds, but told they would loose their deposits.

*BARCO HAS BEEN IN TOUCH WITH PARENTS FROM OTHER GROUPS AS WELL. A NUMBER OF SAD STORIES OF PEOPLE THAT HAD TO RAISE MONEY FOR THEIR KIDS TO GO ON THIS TRIP AND GOT ROBBED IN THE END.

CASE STUDY 2: SARITA DEVCHAND / WENDELL DOMAINGO – HOCKEY GROUP TO NETHERLANDS
 30 kids from various provinces. Departure – 4 December, Return – 13 December
 R38527- most parents paid this amoung – some slight variation in cost – excluded cost of VISA applications.
 95% paid up
 Parents bought thermal clothes – not just the cost of the tour, the clothes, the visas.
 got NOTHING – no flight, no accommodation
o Flight centre cancelled booking – have email from them stating cancellation due to non-payment from Vision Sport
o Accommodation not paid – parents spoke to hotels
ONE PARENT IN GROUP
 One mom is a domestic worker – she paid over R500 the final payment this week – sent a screen shot of payment made, not realizing it showed her balance of just R17 – she literally gave her last money to send her kid on this trip.

CASE STUDY 3: FRANS BESTER – CRICKET TOUR TO SRI LANKA
 Not sure how many kids
 First Departure – June 2019. Postponed to December 2019
 Frans Bester paid R104k in total for his family to accompany his son a cricket tour to Sri Lanka – the cost for his son for the tour was R30700.
 Initially the trip wasn’t cancelled, but postponed because of the April bombings to December 2019.
 Trip officially cancelled a month ago.
 Promised refund, nothing yet.


ADDITIONAL INTERVIEWS
• GROUP OF KIDS
• ASATA – ASSOCIATION OF SOUTHERN AFRICAN TRAVEL AGENTS - Vision Sport is not a member of ASATA – but they will give us an industry perspective.

CONFRONT ☺

• TRYING TO GET PERMISSION TO FILM AT OR – SOME PARENTS & KIDS ARE GOING TO THE AIRPORT ON MONDAY (EVEN THOUGH THE FLIGHTS HAVE NOT BEEN BOOKED)

Script:


STRUCTURE

VO: International school sports tours are all the rage – children from all over South Africa train hard, study hard and aspire to make it onto a team, that will see them jetting off to foreign country - going toe to toe with their overseas counterparts.

LINK: But those dreams were shattered for at four groups of teenagers that were meant to fly out this December. The trips have been cancelled by their tour operator just days before departure.

JONATHAN: All I just wanted to do was go play rugby and I want to play rugby at a high level and that dream didn't materialize,

VO: 16 year old Jonathan Smit was set to leave for Agentina this week , while 17 year old Nick Devchand was heading to the Netherlands for a hockey tournament .

NIKI: It hasn't just been my dream it's been so many other players dreams. To find out that. It Can be done anymore. It's truly a tough thing to digest.

VO: These trips were organized by Vision Sport South Africa, established in 2014. Although not an ASATA member, the company bills itself as a reliable sport and academic tour operator specializing in the planning and professional execution of group travel .

A one-stop travel shop that pulled the plug on a hockey tour to the Netherlands, a cricket tour to Sri Lanka, two rugby tours to Agentina and a soccer tour to the UK - bringing the total paid over to Vision Sport South Africa to over R4 million rand – just for the December cancellations.

The parents are fuming!

HOCKEY VOX3 MOM: I feel so stupid, because I believed in this Vision Sport M1
HOCKEY VOX 1 DAD: Now you get a person like this that stuffs it up for everyone – it’s not on.
APCAN RUGBY VOX 2 DAD: I was very cross. I want to break his fingers, I was very angry

VO: And the kids are devastated.

HOCKEY VOX 1 GIRL: I’ve baking cupcakes to raise money for this tour and now it’s all gone.
HOCKEY VOX2 MOM // no child needs to go through this.
NV RUGBY VOX2 BOY: my hart is gebreek, my vriende se harte is gebreek – ons het geld in gesamel en nou kan ons nie meer gaan nie

VO: The man behind the operation is Michael Byneveldt. According to the website there’s been 105 successful tours – but it seems everything has not been smooth sailing this year.

This clip was secretly recorded during a meeting with parents from the two Rugby groups. Byneveldt claimed he was held hostage by the group.

MICHAEL: // It feels like I am being labelled as a crook and it is really unfair //I have walked so far for people and every day I have been stabbed in the back. //

VO: Byneveldt sent parents a message afterwards, saying he will be closing down the business.

“I will be consulting with our lawyers regarding the legal processes we need to follow to get all outstanding bills paid and to make sure the uncorrupted people gets refunded what is left over after the process.”

Anthony Ncube was selected for the Netherlands Hockey tour. His mom Cynthia says they are still reeling from the dissapointment.

MASA: Cynthia if you could see Michael right now. What would you say.
CYNTHIA: I would strangle him to be honest. //because he has caused so many pain to me.

VO: Cynthia is a domestic worker, the R37900 she raised – did not come easily.

CYNTHIA: // Even in school we survived with bursaries. So. But for him. I always go an extra mile. // because I believe that he can change this situation at home.
MASA What did you have to sacrafice?
CYNTHIA: // I used to ask to work overtime at times. I'll go to the on loan lenders and borrow that money

VO: Interested to get Michael Byneveldt’s side of the story – we went to his offices in Krugersdorp.

LINK: They’ve literally closed their doors. The blinds and windows are shut, it seems Vision Sports South Africa is not operational for now.

VO: Byneveldt declined an interview stating his life has been threatened.

When parents confronted Byneveldt at his home, he appeared defensive and blamed them.

MICHAEL: //julle het die boodskappe op julle fone gebruik – Friday 22 November – Please bring all paymennts up to date – regards Vision Sport Management – Het die mense dit gedoen
PARENT: Myne was op datum
MICHAEL: kan ek vra het almal dit gedoen?

VO: Byneveldt claimed the reason for cancelling the five December trips was that parents have not paid in full, or on time. He claims a total of over R900 000 is still outstanding – the parents dispute this.

MICHAEL: // 80% of you people, of your groups people have not paid on time, it placed me in a financial predicament // So, you can say what you and do what you want from now on. I have had enough.

VO: But that’s not true. While some payments were made late, 95% of the APCAN fees were paid up at the time of cancellation. By the 27th of November – Byneveldt had received R769 000 and still cancelled the trip.

In a last minute letter to Carte Blanche, Byneveld claimed he was forced to refund this group R330 000 – claiming he had already paid oversears service providers.

PARENT: The money you received, where is that?
MICHAEL: That what I had I am trying to pay back and paid to the hotel in Argentina. And used probably.

VO: We have an email from an Agentinian Agent confriming the contrary regarding hotel bookings.

Byneveldt only paid US$5018, which is roughly R73000, towards a hotel booking for the Noordvaal rugby tour// for the APCAN group - not a single cent was paid.

School Group Travel is a small industry – Steven van Zyl has been in the field for 25 years. While Byneveld worked for him years ago, his name has been popping up recently with shared suppliers.

MASA: Does he pay suppliers?
STEVEN: I have facts to prove that he doesn't pay all of them

VO: We have been able to establish that he still owes a Netherlands tour organiser R278000 he also owes a UK based Travel Agency at least R1.2 million rand // dating back to December 2018.

In November, South African Schools Netball President Di Woolley experienced this first hand. She travelled to Singapore with a group of under 15 players. R750 000 was paid in full by their sponsor, the Motsepe Foundation to Vision Sport.

DI: // the money was paid over to him at the end of June. And every time I asked him he said to me no it's been paid, it's been paid it's been paid only to discover that it was not paid.

VO: While Vision Sport booked flights and arranged some transport – over 300 thousand rands worth of ground operations were not paid – including the children accomodation and excursions. Woolley is now liable for those fees.

But this isn’t the first time Byneveldt has let teams down – earlier in 2019 a european athletics tour and a Mauritian netball tour were cancelled just days before departure. In both cases some money has been refunded.

DI: If I'm going to guess it was a question of taking from Peter to pay Paul. // And I think maybe it just snowballed and got to a point where Paul just didn't have any more money to give Peter

VO: Byneveldt states: “I refute the allegations that the parents’ money had been stolen or misappropriated.”

He explained that prices were quoted based on the participation of the whole group and that as per his Ts&Cs - late payments could risk service availibility.

Van Zyl believes blaming parents is ludicrous.

STEVEN: I think he's just using it as an excuse because he doesn't have the money to pay for the services

LINK: The process is pretty straightforward for tour operators – you collect deposits, and you make bookings for the deposits you received – the clients that don’t pay, don’t get bookings and don’t go.

STEVEN: //if 20 people contract with you you are obliged to deliver 20 different contractual services. So if three clients. Would cancel. Services will have to continue for the other 17

VO: But Vision Sport appears to operate differently. Trips were cancelled completely despite most parents paying in full.

Nick Devchand’s mom, Sarita, worked out that more than 93% of the fees were paid by the group when Vision Sport cancelled the Hockey Tour – that’s over R1.1 million .

SARITA: we've sacrificed throughout the year for our kids to go on this tour.

VO: The Noordvaal rugby group paid R978700 – they actually over paid by 1.42% when their tour was cancelled – explains Barco Smit – Jonathan’s father.

BARCO: I don't know how you do that. And then // Cut you tell us that parents haven't come to the party when we've seen that money paid more than we should if more than the budget.

VO: He believes Vision Sport was simply stringing them along, avoiding the inevitable.

BARCO: // He pretend that up to last week that we were still going to fly and that everything was was paid in and everything was correct on his side

VO: In some cases, provisional flight bookings were made and deposits paid over to Flight Centre – but these were cancelled when the balance outstanding did not materialise from Vision Sport South Afrcia.

Some 2020 trips are also hanging in the balance – 3 groups have paid R623 000 in deposits to Vision Sport.

In communication to parents - Byneveldt said the business won’t be closing down any more, stating the situation can be saved.

Although, paying back the money would be the first step towards fixing the situation, some things are irreperable.

STEVEN: // Michael’s taught three to 400 children a lesson in dishonesty and how you can be the victim of it
APCAN RUGBY VOX3: It was our time to shine and now we cant even do that because someone stole the money.


 
PROMOS

PROMO 1
VO: A travel agent specialising in international school sports tours leaves at least 5 groups stranded this December with no flights, no accommodation and no answers.

PROMO 2
VO: Young sports stars expected to jet off on an epic overseas tour but instead, their tour operator cancelled the trip - leaving them out of pocket and with no real explanation.

PROMO 3
VO: A one-stop travel shop promised five groups of children a professionally executed international school tour – but instead the trip got cancelled and they went nowhere.

CYNTHIA: I would strangle him to be honest. //because he has caused so many pain to me. VO: Cynthia is a domestic worker, the R37900 she raised – did not come easily. CYNTHIA: // Even in school we survived with bursaries. So. But for him. I always go an extra mile. // because I believe that he can change this situation at home. MASA What did you have to sacrafice? CYNTHIA: // I used to ask to work overtime at times. I'll go to the on loan lenders and borrow that money VO: Interested to get Michael Byneveldt’s side of the story – we went to his offices in Krugersdorp. LINK: They’ve literally closed their doors. The blinds and windows are shut, it seems Vision Sports South Africa is not operational for now. VO: Byneveldt declined an interview stating his life has been threatened. When parents confronted Byneveldt at his home, he appeared defensive and blamed them. MICHAEL: //julle het die boodskappe op julle fone gebruik – Friday 22 November – Please bring all paymennts up to date – regards Vision Sport Management – Het die mense dit gedoen PARENT: Myne was op datum MICHAEL: kan ek vra het almal dit gedoen? VO: Byneveldt claimed the reason for cancelling the five December trips was that parents have not paid in full, or on time. He claims a total of over R900 000 is still outstanding – the parents dispute this. MICHAEL: // 80% of you people, of your groups people have not paid on time, it placed me in a financial predicament // So, you can say what you and do what you want from now on. I have had enough. VO: But that’s not true. While some payments were made late, 95% of the APCAN fees were paid up at the time of cancellation. By the 27th of November – Byneveldt had received R769 000 and still cancelled the trip. In a last minute letter to Carte Blanche, Byneveld claimed he was forced to refund this group R330 000 – claiming he had already paid oversears service providers. PARENT: The money you received, where is that? MICHAEL: That what I had I am trying to pay back and paid to the hotel in Argentina. And used probably. VO: We have an email from an Agentinian Agent confriming the contrary regarding hotel bookings. Byneveldt only paid US$5018, which is roughly R73000, towards a hotel booking for the Noordvaal rugby tour// for the APCAN group - not a single cent was paid. School Group Travel is a small industry – Steven van Zyl has been in the field for 25 years. While Byneveld worked for him years ago, his name has been popping up recently with shared suppliers. MASA: Does he pay suppliers? STEVEN: I have facts to prove that he doesn't pay all of them VO: We have been able to establish that he still owes a Netherlands tour organiser R278000 he also owes a UK based Travel Agency at least R1.2 million rand // dating back to December 2018. In November, South African Schools Netball President Di Woolley experienced this first hand. She travelled to Singapore with a group of under 15 players. R750 000 was paid in full by their sponsor, the Motsepe Foundation to Vision Sport. DI: // the money was paid over to him at the end of June. And every time I asked him he said to me no it's been paid, it's been paid it's been paid only to discover that it was not paid. VO: While Vision Sport booked flights and arranged some transport – over 300 thousand rands worth of ground operations were not paid – including the children accomodation and excursions. Woolley is now liable for those fees. But this isn’t the first time Byneveldt has let teams down – earlier in 2019 a european athletics tour and a Mauritian netball tour were cancelled just days before departure. In both cases some money has been refunded. DI: If I'm going to guess it was a question of taking from Peter to pay Paul. // And I think maybe it just snowballed and got to a point where Paul just didn't have any more money to give Peter VO: Byneveldt states: “I refute the allegations that the parents’ money had been stolen or misappropriated.” He explained that prices were quoted based on the participation of the whole group and that as per his Ts&Cs - late payments could risk service availibility. Van Zyl believes blaming parents is ludicrous. STEVEN: I think he's just using it as an excuse because he doesn't have the money to pay for the services LINK: The process is pretty straightforward for tour operators – you collect deposits, and you make bookings for the deposits you received – the clients that don’t pay, don’t get bookings and don’t go. STEVEN: //if 20 people contract with you you are obliged to deliver 20 different contractual services. So if three clients. Would cancel. Services will have to continue for the other 17 VO: But Vision Sport appears to operate differently. Trips were cancelled completely despite most parents paying in full. Nick Devchand’s mom, Sarita, worked out that more than 93% of the fees were paid by the group when Vision Sport cancelled the Hockey Tour – that’s over R1.1 million . SARITA: we've sacrificed throughout the year for our kids to go on this tour. VO: The Noordvaal rugby group paid R978700 – they actually over paid by 1.42% when their tour was cancelled – explains Barco Smit – Jonathan’s father. BARCO: I don't know how you do that. And then // Cut you tell us that parents haven't come to the party when we've seen that money paid more than we should if more than the budget. VO: He believes Vision Sport was simply stringing them along, avoiding the inevitable. BARCO: // He pretend that up to last week that we were still going to fly and that everything was was paid in and everything was correct on his side VO: In some cases, provisional flight bookings were made and deposits paid over to Flight Centre – but these were cancelled when the balance outstanding did not materialise from Vision Sport South Afrcia. Some 2020 trips are also hanging in the balance – 3 groups have paid R623 000 in deposits to Vision Sport. In communication to parents - Byneveldt said the business won’t be closing down any more, stating the situation can be saved. Although, paying back the money would be the first step towards fixing the situation, some things are irreperable. STEVEN: // Michael’s taught three to 400 children a lesson in dishonesty and how you can be the victim of it APCAN RUGBY VOX3: It was our time to shine and now we cant even do that because someone stole the money. PROMOS PROMO 1 VO: A travel agent specialising in international school sports tours leaves at least 5 groups stranded this December with no flights, no accommodation and no answers. PROMO 2 VO: Young sports stars expected to jet off on an epic overseas tour but instead, their tour operator cancelled the trip - leaving them out of pocket and with no real explanation. PROMO 3 VO: A one-stop travel shop promised five groups of children a professionally executed international school tour – but instead the trip got cancelled and they went nowhere. metadata.Summary: Vision Sport bills itself as an established and reliable sport/academic tour operator and sport event planner that specializes in the planning and professional execution of the logistics of group travel. A one-stop travel shop. EXCEPT…. They’ve just cancelled 4 different tours, all in for over a R1 million each! Not reliable if you ask me. We speak to kids who’s dreams have been shattered and track down the man that is responsible behind Vision Sport.
metadata.Further information: Michael Byneveldt is behind Vision Sport. The company has been operating since 2014. And a number of tours have taken place. But it hasn’t been smooth sailing in 2019. Tours started getting cancelled in mid-year:  First an athletics tour to Switzerland. R40k per kid. Cancelled three days before departure in June 2019. Refunds never materialised.  Then a cricket tour to Sri Lanka also set for June/July 2019. R30700 per kid. This time not cancelled, but postponed because of the April bombings to December 2019 – cancelled a month ago.  Three groups set to depart now this week – two rugby groups and a hockey group. Each group paid in over R1 million! None of them will be departing. INSIDER I spoke to an employee. She doesn’t want to be interviewed. Says there isn’t enough money in the bank accounts to pay for the tours and that the trips definitely won’t go ahead. Her theory is that Byneveldt is a bad businessman and that he has been under quoting to get the business and then ran into trouble because he had to take from Peter to pay Paul. One of case studies has also spoken to her can relay the story. I have an audio recording. Michael Byneveldt on the other hand likes to blame his clients: “I have decided to close down Vision Sport with immediate effect. It was a very difficult decision to make, considering all the lives that will be effected by this decision. I will be consulting with our lawyers regarding the legal processes we need to follow to get all outstanding bills paid and to make sure the uncorrupted people gets refunded what is left over after the process. It has been a very taxing past 6 years and I have learnt that people are the most unpredictable source of life on this place we call earth. May God be with those who stabbed me and wanted to see me fall. Those who took my kindness for weakness. I forgive you. Thanks to those who held my hand. Even when it went tough. I will stand up. With you and for you. Michael Beyneveldt” On Sunday he sent another message: “Good morning. I have received good movement and support in the past 24 hours regarding the company and how we can save this situation. Vision Sport will still trade as per normal and not be closed down. Unfortunately the tours are ruined, but we are going to see how we can postpone the tours or refund the players after calculating all losses by payments made to service providers. I will be in contact with each one of the parents this week to discuss the options. Best regards Michael” *I HAVE A SECRETLY FILMED VIDEO CLIP OF HIM EXPLAINING HIMSELF TO SOME OF THE PARENTS TAKEN ON THURSDAY WE KNOW WHERE HE IS, HE WILL WANT TO TELL HIS SIDE OF THE STORY BECAUSE HE SAYS PEOPLE DIDN’T PAY ON TIME… BUT THAT’s NOT TRUE CASE STUDY 1: BARCO SMIT GROUP REPRESNETATIVE – NOORDVAAL RUGBY GROUP TO ARGENTINA  23 kids (15/16 years), 3 parents. Departure – 2 December, Return – 11 December  R32400 - 12 November had pay in R5000 – price went up R37400  VISION SPORT blamed parents for not making payment deadlines in a mail on the 18th of October – but after collating all the proof of payments – the parents were actually R40k over on the milestone at that date.  PAID UP IN FULL – accept for R8900 outstanding from two parents. BUT one child got injured and cancelled after paying R25k – so the tour was technically paid up. Cancelled on the 27th November  got NOTHING – no flight, no accommodation o Paid a small deposit for flights to Flight Centre – R9600 still due per person – Flight centre cancelled booking. o Team uniforms and clothing not paid – spoke to supplier o Accommodation not paid – parents spoke to hotels  Promised refunds, but told they would loose their deposits. *BARCO HAS BEEN IN TOUCH WITH PARENTS FROM OTHER GROUPS AS WELL. A NUMBER OF SAD STORIES OF PEOPLE THAT HAD TO RAISE MONEY FOR THEIR KIDS TO GO ON THIS TRIP AND GOT ROBBED IN THE END. CASE STUDY 2: SARITA DEVCHAND / WENDELL DOMAINGO – HOCKEY GROUP TO NETHERLANDS  30 kids from various provinces. Departure – 4 December, Return – 13 December  R38527- most parents paid this amoung – some slight variation in cost – excluded cost of VISA applications.  95% paid up  Parents bought thermal clothes – not just the cost of the tour, the clothes, the visas.  got NOTHING – no flight, no accommodation o Flight centre cancelled booking – have email from them stating cancellation due to non-payment from Vision Sport o Accommodation not paid – parents spoke to hotels ONE PARENT IN GROUP  One mom is a domestic worker – she paid over R500 the final payment this week – sent a screen shot of payment made, not realizing it showed her balance of just R17 – she literally gave her last money to send her kid on this trip. CASE STUDY 3: FRANS BESTER – CRICKET TOUR TO SRI LANKA  Not sure how many kids  First Departure – June 2019. Postponed to December 2019  Frans Bester paid R104k in total for his family to accompany his son a cricket tour to Sri Lanka – the cost for his son for the tour was R30700.  Initially the trip wasn’t cancelled, but postponed because of the April bombings to December 2019.  Trip officially cancelled a month ago.  Promised refund, nothing yet. ADDITIONAL INTERVIEWS • GROUP OF KIDS • ASATA – ASSOCIATION OF SOUTHERN AFRICAN TRAVEL AGENTS - Vision Sport is not a member of ASATA – but they will give us an industry perspective. CONFRONT ☺ POSSIBLE INTERVIEW • FLIGHT CENTRE? Will ask – not sure if they’ll do it. • TRYING TO GET PERMISSION TO FILM AT OR – SOME PARENTS & KIDS ARE GOING TO THE AIRPORT ON MONDAY (EVEN THOUGH THE FLIGHTS HAVE NOT BEEN BOOKED)
